testSelectors: test/workspaces/view-replay.test.ts#ViewReplayProtocol [C13-VIEW-DELTA-REPLAY] delegates RFC 6902 and durably replays deltas
bounds: This rule does not promise that every cursor a client ever held still resumes. Resume resolves a presented EventCursor against the stored Views and ViewDeltas of its own stream, so a cursor whose revision a host has since compacted away no longer names a position and is refused rather than silently restarted. Compaction is the host's own administrative choice over its own storage, and the refusal is what keeps a resumed position honest instead of substituting a position the client never held. A retired stream is unaffected: its terminal View is the one revision compaction cannot delete.

remainingEvidence: A View stream is now the pair of a SurfaceId and the SurfaceEpoch its registration assigned. View carries the terminal field and ViewDelta carries the epoch, both at bumped codec majors with no reader left for the previous ones. Retirement emits exactly one terminal ViewDelta whose cursor is the base View's own, because that patch consumes no Event, and every later snapshot or delta for that epoch is refused by reading the terminal View rather than a second liveness flag.

An epoch belongs to a registration rather than to a retirement. WorkspacePersistence requires a current SurfaceRegistration for the exact SurfaceId before a stream opens and before any revision advances, so retirement alone cannot open epoch 2 and only a reinstallation can. currentSurfaceEpoch derives the next epoch from the stored Views, which compaction cannot delete for a retired epoch, so a later PackagePin registering the same static SurfaceId opens a fresh stream at the next epoch while every earlier terminal View stays readable at the revision it ended on.

Resume is keyed on the opaque EventCursor the record defines, not on a revision a client would have to derive. ViewReplayProtocol.replay resolves a presented cursor against the stored Views and deltas of that exact stream, refuses an unknown cursor and a cursor of another stream by name, and yields a retired epoch's terminal revision through the same reader live resume uses. A client detects retirement from the returned View alone, holding no live handle.

The aggregating conjunct is NOT claimed and its owner is outside this wave, but its call-into-this-plane half is no longer missing. §6.3 requires an aggregating Surface to drop a retired child's entry at its next revision, and no production Surface composes the surface-backed slot entries §4.2 describes. The withdrawal path does now reach this plane and is exercised end to end: src/composition/facet-withdrawal.ts retires the SurfaceRegistrations of one exact contribution, which terminates each stream through WorkspacePersistence.retireSurfaceRegistration at the epoch that registration assigned, and a later PackagePin re-registering the same static SurfaceId opens the next epoch — evidenced by C13-FACET-WITHDRAWAL-EXACT's own W3-owned case, which requireEvidenceOwner keeps out of this row's selectors. What is still owed is only the composition of child Views from contributor attribution; a helper that composed them existed here with no production caller and was deleted rather than left standing as evidence, because AGENTS.md requires an unimplemented piece to be absent instead of fake.

The row cannot rise above implemented for a second, independent reason, though that reason has shrunk. Its prerequisite C13-FACET-WITHDRAWAL-EXACT is W3-owned and still implemented — its authority, Surface-retirement and retained-ContentRef items have closed, and what remains there is W0's mutation campaign over the exact head plus maintainer review — and the ledger refuses a verified row whose prerequisite is unverified.

Recorded discrimination is owed and is not this row's to write. artifacts/quality/discrimination/ is W0-owned and holds no attribution file for src/workspaces, so nothing can judge whether these citations constrain SurfaceEpoch, the terminal refusals, the registration requirement, currentSurfaceEpoch, or the cursor resume path. Promotion needs a W7 mutation run recording a symbol-tier kill inside each.
bounds: This rule does not claim which Facet withdrawal retires which Surface. That membership is C13-FACET-WITHDRAWAL-EXACT's mechanism; the citation here is the retirement path a withdrawal calls, because the discriminator is what terminality and re-registration decide.
